transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-16
Start: 08:30 AM PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (CTO, Verdure Systems), Luis Martinez (ML Engineer), Priya Singh (Infra Lead), Evan Boyd (PM)

Summary:
Quick discovery covering Verdure's time-to-first-token (TTFT) needs, quickstart credits, and the decision criteria between Hosted (PLG) vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC. Customer emphasized latency SLOs for interactive editor and strict data residency + SOC2 compliance for PII-adjacent logs. Agreed next steps: security pack, credits provision, and SE bench session.

Topics Covered:
- Current stack and constraints (Kubernetes, Redis, internal model fallback)
- Typical inference patterns (editor completions, reranking, embeddings for search)
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs and expected QPS
- Hosted quickstart and credits to validate TTFT
- Dedicated reserved capacity options and pilot SOW triggers
- Compliance items (SOC2, KMS, audit logs, data retention)

Action items (recapped at end of call):
- Maya to send pricing & credits, security pack (SOC2)
- Devon to run bench script with requested token lengths
- Priya to share traffic profile and compliance constraints

--- Transcript (timestamps ~every 30-60s, note: auto-transcript contains small mis-hearings) ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I'm Maya, I'm the AE at Redwood, and with me is Devon, our solutions engineer. How's everyone?
[00:12] Anika Rao: Morning Maya, thanks. I'm Anika, CTO here at Verdure. I've got Luis, Priya and Evan with me.
[00:20] Devon Park: Great, quick agenda — we'll spend 10 minutes hearing about your use case and constraints, then talk TTFT/credits and hosting options, and finish with next steps. Does that work?
[00:29] Anika Rao: Yep, sounds good. We're primarily exploring a quick path to production for an in-app co-editing assistant and a document search reranker. Need to understand cost and latency.
[00:40] Luis Martinez: We're on k8s, have Redis for session state, and current internal LLM is on-prem but slow for interactive.
[00:50] Priya Singh: Also need to check data residency — logs containing PII fields need to stay in our EU tenant. SOC2 is a blocker for procurement.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Totally — those are common. For TTFT we have a self-serve Redwood API with free credits to validate latency and quality. Most teams get to first token inside an hour after the credit grant and quickstart steps.
[01:20] Evan Boyd: When you say "first token in an hour" is that assuming we use the SDK? We want to embed it into our editor flow quickly.
[01:28] Devon Park: Yes, we have SDKs and quickstart templates. Typical path: sign up, get API key, run quickstart example for completions and embeddings, then swap in your prompt and traffic patterns. We'll give you a sample harness to replicate your seq lengths and batching.
[01:45] Anika Rao: How do you isolate data during the quickstart? We don't want logs shipped out.
[01:52] Maya Chen: The hosted API can be configured to not persist request/response content for evaluation — and for enterprise we offer Dedicated and Private where you can control retention and bring your own KMS. We'll add the SOC2 docs showing these options.
[02:11] Luis Martinez: P95 latency target for the editor is 250ms on 512 token completions. Is that realistic on hosted?
[02:19] Devon Park: For that target, it depends on model choice and batching. On our high-throughput hosted tiers we can hit sub-200ms p95 on optimized small-medium models for 512 tokens with continuous batching turned off for low-latency paths. If you need consistent 250ms at scale, Dedicated with reserved capacity is most predictable.
[02:40] Maya Chen: Also there are model variants we route to when capacity tightens to keep latency SLOs — those are documented in the performance profiles.
[02:49] Priya Singh: Can Dedicated be in our VPC? We need traffic to never traverse public internet.
[02:56] Devon Park: Yes, Dedicated can be set up with a private endpoint inside your VPC and we also do Private deployments for full on-prem or air-gapped setups. The Dedicated VPC option gives you predictable throughput without full private install.
[03:10] Anika Rao: Ok that's helpful. Cost wise, how should we think about credits -> pilot -> dedicated?
[03:18] Maya Chen: We usually grant credits to validate realistic token usage. After the quickstart you can run a 2–4 week pilot on Hosted to measure cost/latency. If you hit the thresholds you define (e.g., sustained 50 rps with <300ms p95) we help scope a Dedicated reserve and draft a pilot SOW.
[03:36] Evan Boyd: Are there any gotchas for our embeddings use case? We plan to do nightly reindexes and online low-latency similarity search.
[03:46] Devon Park: For nightly bulk embeddings you can leverage batch/throughput-optimized kernels — that's cost efficient. For online similarity search we recommend caching vectors in your embedding store (you mentioned Redis) and serving embeddings from a low-latency model variant; we'll show how to use prefix/kv cache and caching TTLs to reduce calls.
[04:05] Luis Martinez: You mentioned KV cache — our infra people call it K-V cash sometimes — I always trip when docs use weird terms.
[04:12] Maya Chen: [laughs] we get that in transcripts. We'll send a bench doc that explains KV cache, prefix caching and how it affects token cost.
[04:22] Anika Rao: About compliance: we need proof of SOC2, encryption at rest, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Does Redwood support forwarding audit logs?
[04:33] Devon Park: Yes, audit logs can be exported to your SIEM in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we also provide audit log exports and long-term retention as an add-on. KMS integration is available for Private and Dedicated to meet your key control policies.
[04:50] Priya Singh: For the quickstart, will we get EU-region hosting? Our data residency policy requires EU processing.
[04:58] Maya Chen: We have hosted regions in EU; credits can be provisioned for an EU account region. We'll confirm regional availability in the pack we send.
[05:08] Evan Boyd: Any risk of model quality drift when you route to fallback variants during capacity events? We rely on consistent outputs.
[05:16] Devon Park: Good question. We document compatibility matrices and provide automatic fallback policies that prefer same-architecture variants to reduce behavioral drift. Additionally Redwood Optimize can surface regressions tied to your eval prompt sets so you can detect behavior changes.
[05:33] Anika Rao: How long does it typically take to set up a Dedicated pilot if we decide after the quickstart?
[05:40] Maya Chen: From contract and infra clearance maybe 2–6 weeks depending on procurement and VPC setup; technically the infra provisioning is quick but SSO, KMS and security reviews add time. We'll include a sample SOW timeline.
[05:54] Luis Martinez: For benching, can we run a custom script to simulate editor traffic (a lot of small completions) and a reranker for larger context?
[06:03] Devon Park: Absolutely — we'll provide a benchmark harness. I'll include scripts for variable seq lengths, synthetic KV cache warm-up and a production-like traffic profile. We can run the bench live with you or share results.
[06:18] Anika Rao: What do you need from us to get started?
[06:22] Maya Chen: Three things: a short traffic profile (qps, avg sequence length, peak), a security contact to receive SOC2 docs, and a PO or acceptance that credits are fine for initial evaluation.
[06:33] Priya Singh: I'll share the traffic profile and security contact. Procurement will need SOC2 and a data processing addendum.
[06:40] Evan Boyd: If the quickstart looks good, we'd like to run a 3-week pilot and then agree on a Dedicated sizing by month four.
[06:49] Maya Chen: That fits our usual playbook. We'll provision 30k credits to start, send step-by-step quickstart, security pack, and a TTFT guide.
[06:59] Devon Park: I'll prepare the bench harness and a runbook for running the 8k token / 512 token editor tests and a reranker scenario.
[07:09] Anika Rao: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:12] Luis Martinez: Wondering if you have any public perf numbers for 512 token p95 on hosted and dedicated to cite in our doc?
[07:20] Devon Park: We'll attach the performance profile PDF. Quick note: hosted p95 can range between 150–400ms for 512 tokens based on model and tenant tier; dedicated is much tighter and we can give a SLO-backed threshold.
[07:34] Priya Singh: Also need guidance on costs for embeddings at nightly scale vs online low-latency — a model recommendation would help.
[07:41] Maya Chen: We'll recommend a split: small/medium embedding model for nightly bulk, and a low-latency variant for online. We'll include estimated cost examples with the credits.
[07:55] Anika Rao: Awesome. Let's recap next steps.
[07:58] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya to send security pack + SOC2 checklist, credits and quickstart steps (due 2026-01-18). Devon to prepare benchmark harness and runbook (due 2026-01-21). Priya to share traffic profile and security contact (due 2026-01-20). Schedule bench session for week of 2026-01-20.
[08:20] Evan Boyd: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:23] Anika Rao: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:26] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and docs. Bye.

End of transcript.
